description.narrative:
During the IJET PMU field visit to Cambodia from October 7–10, 2025, Oxfam in Cambodia was informed that additional funding is available to supplement the currently approved budget for implementing the Cambodia Just Energy Transition. This funding is intended to strengthen efforts, particularly those focused on promoting community-owned renewable energy initiatives and contributing to promoting gender and inclusive energy transition.
Recognizing the potential to scale up existing community-led energy systems, enhance theparticipation of women and youth in the clean energy sector, and address the urgent need to promote green loan products within Cambodia’s financial institutions, Oxfam in Cambodia has proposed two new activities and an expanded activity to be integrated into the approved workplan. These additions aim to better support vulnerable communities in adapting to climate change and advancing a just and inclusive energy transition across the country and contributing to Outcome 3 of IJET by mobilizing finance to support the promotion of Community Owned Renewable Energy (CORE) at the same time linkage with other Oxfam regional projects such as 1/ Fair Finance Assia by working with financial institutions to promote green loans product to gear uptheir investment in clean energy and 2/ Mekong Water Governance by strengthening capacity of water user groups to advocate for better irrigation water governance plan of the Cambodia government.
Enhance the capacity and scale of community-owned renewable energy models in Cambodia towards showcasing its viability and attracting more investments for expansion and replication, Timeframe: January – June 2026, with funding allocation: USD 20,000 Implementation by Solar Green Energy (Cambodia) Co., Ltd.
Contribute to outcome #3: Increased private and public funding for community-owned gender and socially inclusive renewable energy initiatives: The support will enhance and scale-up a community-owned renewable energy model at the Wattamim Commune in Batambang Province by enhancing community capacity in project management (including income generation and financial management)scaling up the capacity of the solar irrigation system in terms of volume and coverage and facilitate the introduction of value adding activities that will optimize the use of generated power. This model will serve as compelling evidence on how community-led renewable energy can boost community income, foster green job creation, and promote sustainable development that can be leveraged in mobilizing additional investments for expanding the CORE model in other communities.

participating-org.narrative:
"Solar Green Energy (Cambodia) Co., Ltd called “SOGE”, was legally registered in December 2013 to work in Renewable Energy Sector especially in Solar Energy field. SOGE was first founded as an association named” Renewable Energy Development Association (REDA)” in2008. The goal of this association was to increase the use of green energy in rural Cambodia. Now, SOGE provides high quality and standard products and services with highest responsibility. SOGE sell all kind of Solar system such as Solar off <(>&<)> on Grid, Solar Water Pump, Solar Hybrid Solar Back-Up system and smart farm system in the green house.
With the economic growth of 7% in Cambodia, the electricity demand increases 10% each year since 2010. For reduction of low electrification rate and high price of electricity in Cambodia, SOGE exists to unleash the full potential of the development of solar energy and obligates to bring benefits of green environment to people across the country. To date, we become an importer, manufacturer and maintenance service provider.
SOGE vision is to become number one of renewable energy technology company in Cambodia. SOGE focuses on the manufacturing and distributing high quality products, and providing technical support, maintenance services and innovation of renewable energy in Cambodia."
